text: Cole names the seven-part path from niche selection through multi-model monetization.
Thirty daily publications create both a library and 30 demand data points.
Audit jobs, hobbies, and lived experiences for existing working knowledge.
Take the top three to five knowledge advantages and test them through public writing.
Small within-account outliers are treated as directional demand signals.
Use social distribution to build a content library and move interested readers to owned email.
Social, newsletter, and offer should address the same topic and problem at increasing depth.
A simpler, more congruent supply chain reduces drop-off between content, email, and offer.
Choose an offer using skill fit and the time horizon for making money.
Cole recommends beginning with a bounded digital product or a recurring service before adding more complex models.
The first revenue prerequisite is having a product or service available for sale.
The first payment begins the customer-feedback and product-improvement cycle.
Customer interviews reveal confusion, missing value, willingness to pay, questions, and purchase reasons.
Feedback either improves the existing offer or exposes a distinct problem for a separate upsell.
Scale by selling the same offer to more people or more offers to the same people.
A mature portfolio serves different customer needs and price points through multiple offer types.
